plimsoll trainer · 10 / advisory evidence

Efficiency advisor

An agent adds up a column by fetching 128 rows one at a time. The agent cannot see that; it wrote a loop that works. The customer's API cannot see it; it served 128 valid requests. The broker in the middle saw all 128, with their route template and timing, because it was already checking each one. The advisor is that view, read after the run, from metadata and nothing else.

02

What one row holds, and what it cannot

The struck-through rows are not redacted. They have no field to live in, so nothing downstream of the trace can hold them either: not a finding, not the caller hint, not the audit record, not the metrics.

  • Method, RouteThe verb and the matched route template, such as GET /items/*: the string from the operator's own profile, never the path the guest sent.
  • Status, DeliveredThe upstream status, and whether the broker handed the response to the guest. A capped or unreadable body keeps its row, marked undelivered, so a 200 the guest never saw is not counted as a record retrieved.
  • Bytes, LatencyRequest and response sizes, and the round trip. Sizes only, so a repeated read of the same size cannot be told apart from a changed one, which is why that detector caps its severity.
  • Denied, Shed, DroppedCounts kept beside the rows: refused by policy, shed by the breaker, and rows past the 256-row cap, which makes a count say "at least".
  • PathNo field. /items/8813 is never recorded; only the template it matched.
  • Query, BodyNo field. Not the request body, not the response body, not a query value.
  • CredentialNo field. The minted token lives in Go and is attached upstream of the trace.
  • Start timeNo field. Rows have durations, not timestamps, so the trace cannot tell serial calls from concurrent ones. A "sequential calls" detector was deleted for exactly that reason, along with an "aggregate in code" one that would have needed the row data.

The one thing that answers "so you just record less". A caller may stamp an opaque trace_id on the run; the daemon echoes it onto the audit line and does nothing else with it. The path and the body then exist in exactly one place, one layer up, in the caller's own log, joinable by that id. That is the difference between recording less and recording only the part that is ours.

03

Who may see it, and what is kept

Two profile settings, orthogonal to each other. advice decides who can act; advice_retention decides what reaches the durable audit log. plimsoll stores nothing itself, so retention is about what it emits.
